HackNation 2026 · AED Mission – Data to the Rescue

Every minute counts

Every AED owner publishes its own list of devices on dane.gov.pl and is responsible for keeping it up to date. The lists merge into one nationwide list, so that anyone can find the nearest available device in seconds.

  • Find the nearest AEDA map with opening hours and whether the device is accessible.

Problem

In sudden cardiac arrest every minute counts, and anyone can use an AED. But you need to know where the nearest one is, whether it is accessible and whether it works. Today's AED lists cannot promise that, because no one is responsible for them.

  • Scattered

    Several databases, each kept separately and in its own format.

  • Unverified

    Opening hours and contacts are missing. It is unclear who last checked a device, and when.

  • No one responsible

    Lists are kept by third parties, not by the owners. When the data is wrong, no one answers for it.

See the solution

Frequently asked questions about AEDs

What is an AED defibrillator?

An AED (automated external defibrillator) is a portable device that analyses the heart rhythm of a person in sudden cardiac arrest and delivers an electric shock if needed. It guides the rescuer step by step with voice prompts.

Who can use an AED?

Anyone, even without training. The AED checks the heart rhythm itself and only delivers a shock when one is needed. Before you use it, call the emergency number 112 and start chest compressions.

How do I find the nearest AED?

Call 112 – the dispatcher can point you to the nearest available device. AED Radar will show the nearest defibrillators on a map with their opening hours and whether they are accessible. The map prototype is coming soon.

How do I add a defibrillator to the AED database?

If you own an AED (a municipality, school, company or fire brigade), you can add it in a form or import a CSV or GeoJSON file. It takes a few minutes. Write to us: kontakt@hacknation-2026.pl.

Where can I find open data on AED defibrillators?

We are preparing a single AED dataset for publication on dane.gov.pl, the Polish open data portal, in CSV and GeoJSON. Every record will state its source and last verification date, and the data can be reused in your own apps and maps.
